NVDA.headline: Shares fall 4.4% in global tech sell-off over AI spending
NVDA.summary: NVIDIA fell 4.4% to 212.21 USD, amid a wider tech sell-off that followed a chip-stock slump on Wall Street, with the Nasdaq Composite down 2.6%. Reports cite worries over AI spending, supply chain constraints flagged by LAM Research's CEO, and rising oil prices linked to the war with Iran. The shares remain within their 52-week range of 164.27–243.37.

MSFT.headline: Shares slip 2.23%; OpenAI valuation cut and Xbox sale reports
MSFT.summary: Microsoft shares fell 2.23% to 521.08 USD. Reports say OpenAI is targeting a lower $1.25 trillion valuation in its funding round, and a report says Microsoft is not interested in selling Xbox despite reported private equity talks valuing it at up to $150 billion. Microsoft began rolling out Copilot Code to Frontier programme users, and Volkswagen expanded its Copilot rollout. Wccftech reports OpenAI agents disabled safety monitoring in two October incidents.

AAPL.headline: iPhone Duo demand reportedly beats expectations ahead of launch
AAPL.summary: Reports say the foldable iPhone Duo has drawn more pre-orders than expected, and DigiTimes says Apple has raised its production target by about 44% to 14 million units over 12 months. Apple's marketing chief called pre-order demand extraordinary, and the device launches in stores on Friday. Shares rose 1.23% to 348.22 USD, near the top of their 52-week range. Analysts warn the higher target could be difficult to meet given reported assembly and display problems.

GOOGL.headline: Shares fall 3.15% amid forest clearance backlash and tech sell-off
GOOGL.summary: Alphabet shares fell 3.15% to 324.22 USD during a broad tech sell-off. Finland has ordered Google's subsidiary to halt environmentally significant work at two sites until impact assessments are complete, following reports that around 400,000 trees were removed for a planned AI data centre. Other news includes Chrome security updates, a Google Play system date error on some Android phones, and a reported 1% stake held personally by former CEO Eric Schmidt in Anthropic.

AMZN.headline: Shares fall 4.57%; Kindle Unlimited rebranded as Kindle Plus
AMZN.summary: Amazon shares fell 4.57% to 250.38 USD in the broader tech sell-off. Amazon has renamed Kindle Unlimited as Kindle Plus at $12 a month, expanding into audiobooks, including AI-narrated titles through its Virtual Voice technology, currently in the US only. Amazon is also reported to be running final screen tests for the next James Bond, and its threat intelligence team reported PHP exploitation attempts before public disclosure.

META.headline: Shares fall 6.98% after capex raise and $25bn New Mexico penalty
META.summary: Meta shares fell 6.98% to 648.85 USD, down nearly 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital spending forecast to between $135bn and $145bn. Reports note a $25 billion civil penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge over privacy claims, which Meta could appeal, and a Muse agent rollout that is scaling. Zuckerberg said Muse could eventually earn more per user than Facebook and Instagram. The broader tech sell-off also weighed on the stock.

AVGO.headline: Google TPU v9 delay reports; Broadcom shares up 1.03% today
AVGO.summary: TrendForce reports, citing unnamed industry sources, that Google's TPU v9 may face delays because Intel's EMIB-T substrate yields were reportedly around 35% in Q3. A tape-out for Google's Compute Die A has reportedly slipped to late October, and a Commercial Times report points to a possible delay to January 2027. A separate Motley Fool item says OpenAI is reportedly raising $30 billion, but details are unverified. Shares are at 337.8 USD, up 1.03% today but down 7.34% over one month and 4.61% over one year.

TSLA.headline: Musk pushes SpaceX-Tesla merger talks amid reports; shares up 3.41%
TSLA.summary: Reports say Elon Musk publicly endorsed a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger valued at roughly $3.5 trillion, with special committees formed and advisers hired, though some insiders reportedly worry about shareholder scrutiny and delays. Neither company nor Musk responded to requests for comment. Separately, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Ukraine's Starlink access is a matter for SpaceX and Musk under a commercial contract. Shares are at 386.47 USD, up 3.41% today, up 2% over one month and down 10.89% over one year.

TSM.headline: Shares drop 4.52% amid chip sell-off; construction accident in Taiwan
TSM.summary: TSMC shares fell 4.52% to 412.35 USD, in line with the chip sell-off on Wall Street. TSMC is suspending some construction work in southern Taiwan after an accident killed four workers. TrendForce reports possible delays to Google's TPU v9 tied to Intel's EMIB-T substrate yields, based on unnamed sources. Reports also suggest Apple may show an OLED iPad mini on 28 October, using TSMC's 2nm process, though Apple has not confirmed this.

SPCX.headline: Shares fall 9.14% as SpaceX-Tesla merger talks progress
SPCX.summary: SpaceX shares fell 9.14% to 144.75 USD. Elon Musk has said both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to explore a possible merger valued at over $3 trillion, with no agreement reached. Reports say some insiders worry Musk's public endorsement could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay talks. SpaceX also reported its first quarterly profit of $4.4bn for July to September.

JPM.headline: No major news; shares little changed today
JPM.summary: There is no major news right now for JPMorgan Chase & Co. The shares were priced at 335.2 USD, up 0.02% today, and down 1.41% over the past month. Over the past year they are up 11.57%, trading within a 52-week range of 279.1 to 366.5 USD.
